ops.d: List every dnsZones in the subscription.
List the dnsZones in a resource group.

features.t: DNS zones (create, get, list, delete) over ARM
Private DNS zones (zoneType = Private, no public name servers)
x: Vyomi models public and private zones as the SAME ARM resource (Microsoft.Network/dnszones) distinguished by properties.zoneType, matching this core's shape — real Azure exposes private zones as a separate resource type (Microsoft.Network/privateDnsZones) with its own API. A zone's type is fixed at creation.

features.t: Record sets (A, AAAA, CAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, SOA, SRV, TXT) — create, get, list, update, delete
x: DS, NAPTR and TLSA record sets round-trip over the native API/CLI (az network dns record-set ds|naptr|tlsa) but, matching the real portal, have no Record set type option in this console's Add/Edit dialog.

Vyomi stores each zone's registration and resolution virtual networks as the two plain ARM-ref lists this core models (same shape as the real zone resource's own properties), not as separate Microsoft.Network/privateDnsZones/virtualNetworkLinks child resources — so a link has no independent name, provisioning state or autoRegistration flag of its own, and DNS resolution/auto-registration from a linked virtual network's VMs is not modelled.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this DNS zone
x: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this DNS zone only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a DNS zone is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the DNS zone itself.

Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

Check access, Role assignments and Deny assignments are REAL and scoped to this DNS zone's resource id: Check access runs core/azure_iam_core.py's evaluator (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group), the lists filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers it, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Principal IDs are free text (Vyomi has no real directory); 'My access' and Classic administrators stay honest gaps. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.
The Export template tab is the shared ARM/Bicep/Terraform export (azure.common.export_template), generated from the properties Vyomi stores for the zone.
The guided DNS diagnostic tiles are not modelled.
